officer.subject: Your under-borrowed position, and where the 10-year has gone since March
officer.body:
Hi Marc,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Below are some thoughts on your TMSS 2026/27 that went to full Council on 5 March. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your strategy is unusually explicit about scenarios, and section 8.2.4 is more candid than most about the reserves position underneath the internal borrowing; this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The starting point is section 8.1: the under-borrowed position is prudent because medium and longer dated borrowing rates are expected to fall from their current levels. Table 1 has MUFG's central path with the 10-year PWLB certainty rate at 5.20% for March 2026, easing to 4.70% by December 2027. As of 12 August the 10-year certainty rate is around 5.80% — roughly 0.6% above the March starting level, not below it. Bank Rate has already landed on the 3.75% Table 1 assumed for March, so one leg of the forecast is in place, but the long end has moved the other way. Postponement can still be the right call if the fall comes later; it makes each quarterly review point material rather than routine, since Table 6 has external borrowing growing from £131.7m at 31 March 2026 to £149.1m base or £157.2m ambitious by 2027/28.

Section 8.2.4 is where most councils understate what you spell out. Reading Table 5 alongside Table 6, internal borrowing was £30.3m at 2024/25 outturn, an estimated £24.7m at 31 March 2026, and drops to £20.7m by 2030/31 base case (£18.3m ambitious). So there's daylight between the pace at which the CFR grows and the pace at which external borrowing catches up, and it maps onto the reserves point exactly. Our monthly sector data at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity shows what borrowing this size looks like as it comes to market, which is worth watching before you draw rather than after.

One thing about your existing book we can price today, offered as information not advice. Three long-dated PWLB loans at 2.20%, 2.24% and 2.49% total £31.2m and run to 2065-2069 — 26% of the book at rates that aren't on the current curve at any tenor. On the DMO's premature repayment curve (notice 314/26 PM, 14 August) those three sit well below par, and the loan book as a whole prices to a net indicative discount of £17.8m against a £117.1m balance — 29 loans below par, 31 above, priced daily at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. These are indicative and only the DMO's quote is binding; we model no MRP or accounting treatment; and whether anything is worth doing turns on replacement cost we don't model. The number is offered so you can see what your book looks like on today's curve, not as a suggestion to move.

The piece of the CIPFA 2021 Prudential Code we'd flag as a resource is the liability benchmark. Our interactive pathway is built on live data and is worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the updated Prudential and Treasury Codes.

On training, four look most relevant to Anglesey: Strategic PWLB borrowing, for the roughly £35m of extra external borrowing under the base case across the plan period (up to £98m ambitious); MRP policy, since yours is asset-life annuity priced off your own average rate on all loans; HRA treasury and financing, for the HRA CFR climbing from £35.7m in 2026/27 to £93.3m by 2030/31 under ambitious; and the liability benchmark pathway. For members, Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) is written for exactly the Governance & Audit committee that scrutinised this paper on 4 February. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
